## 技术雷达 · 北京时间 2026-11-22

今日最重要的变化是：机器人 VLA 开始引入时间有序的神经动作 tokenizer 实现流式动作解码，同时推理系统侧围绕可变形状多模态 encoder、混合循环层、投机解码与动态 batch 的多个 PR 集中出现，反映出从“吞吐优先”向“首 token/动作延迟、尾延迟与动态形状”的转向。以下按研究点展开，所有材料均为 GitHub PR 或代码提交原文，未做独立复现。

---

**1. NAT VLA：时间有序动作 tokenizer 实现流式动作执行**  
- **原始材料**：`[huggingface/lerobot PR] feat(policies): add the NAT VLA policy (nat_vla)`，发布日期 2026-11-21，GitHub PR，URL：https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/5416  
- **旧问题**：经典 VLA 通常一次生成固定长度的动作 chunk，机器人必须等整个 chunk 解码完成才能执行，首动作延迟高，不利于 30 Hz 或更高的控制闭环。  
- **核心技术机制**：引入 NAT（neural action tokenizer），将动作序列编码为时间有序 token，且 decoder 保持因果结构——一个 chunk 的前几个动作 token 可以先解码并执行，剩余仍在生成。LeRobot 策略基于 LFM2-VL，`select_action` 在后台线程贪婪生成，每个 latent 对应动作 token 生成后立刻返回；可选 `--policy.rtc_steps` 实现 token-prefix real-time chunking，在当前 chunk 最后几个动作执行期间预生成下一 chunk，并用这些 token 作为前缀。  
- **与已有路线差别**：不同于等整个 action chunk 解码完再执行或非因果的 token 排列，NAT 利用时间因果性把动作 chunk 变成可流式前缀，降低首动作可见延迟。  
- **可信程度**：PR body 自述，含 24 个单元测试；在 LIBERO 帧上复现训练 loss（7.621155 vs 7.621157）；RTX 4090 首动作约 40 ms；30 Hz 循环中 chunk 切换动作变化从 0.05–0.10 降到 0.011–0.031；100 步 fine-tune 通过。但权重和 tokenizer 尚未公开，且未报告真实机器人任务成功率；本文未核验全文。  
- **启示**：对 VLA 推理，时间有序动作 token 提供了一种类似 LLM streaming 的“部分 chunk 可执行”机制，直接攻击首动作延迟；异步控制上后台线程生成与 RTC 适合多线程控制循环，但需验证部分执行动作与后续生成 token 的一致性；对任务成功率/时间目前缺少证据，必须用标准 manipulation benchmark 补充闭环成功率；对 GPU 推理系统，动作解码的流式返回与 continuous batching 调度存在类比，可按 token 粒度调度优先级。

---

**2. LFM3-VL encoder CUDA Graph：可变分辨率卷积的图化**  
- **原始材料**：`[vllm-project/vllm PR] [MM][CG] Add encoder CUDA graph support for LFM3-VL`，发布日期 2026-11-19，GitHub PR，URL：https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67976  
- **旧问题**：LFM3-VL 视觉 encoder 将注意力与 2D depthwise 卷积交错，输入是任意原生分辨率 `(H,W)` 网格，无法用固定 shape 捕获 CUDA Graph，导致 prefill 阶段难以图化、TTFT 偏高。  
- **核心技术机制**：在 graph 外预计算 1-based 空间邻居索引 `conv_indices`（LRU 缓存），graph 内运行一个 fused Triton gather-conv2d kernel，使任意 aspect ratio 共享同一个 1D token-budget graph 集合，避免为每个分辨率捕获独立 graph；支持 image、multi-image、video。  
- **与已有路线差别**：此前 LFM3-VL encoder 只能走 eager 路径；本 PR 使用“预计算索引 + fused gather-conv”把可变 2D 形状归一化到固定 token-budget 的 graph 集，且保持数值完全一致。  
- **可信程度**：PR body 自述，包含 pytest 测试通过、端到端 `vllm bench serve` 600 reqs/mode 数据：Mean TTFT 53.02→38.55 ms（-27.3%），P99 TTFT 111.10→65.90 ms（-40.7%），MMStar 120 样本 accuracy 56.67%→57.50%。数据来自作者环境，未独立复现；本文未核验全文。  
- **启示**：对 GPU 推理系统，该设计为动态形状多模态输入提供可图化范式——把不规则维度外推到索引/预算层，用单一 fused kernel 消除 shape 特化；VLA 常接收多相机或视频流，若使用 VL encoder，该方法可降低感知延迟，提高闭环频率；异步控制里传感器帧的分辨率/数量动态变化，需要类似 runtime shape 支持；对机器人任务成功率/时间，目前无直接证据，须在真实机器人感知-控制链路测量端到端收益。

---

**3. GDN MTP decode kernel 针对 16-bit recurrent state 的融合优化**  
- **原始材料**：`[vllm-project/vllm PR] [Kernel][GDN] Faster fused CUDA MTP decode for 16-bit recurrent state`，发布日期 2026-11-21，GitHub PR，URL：https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69065  
- **旧问题**：在 16-bit（BF16/FP16）recurrent state 下，现有 fused GDN MTP decode kernel 受 warp-shuffle reduction 限制，带宽仅约 1.9–3.6 TB/s；FP16 状态甚至被迫 fallback 到 Triton，无法享受 fused CUDA kernel。  
- **核心技术机制**：新 fused CUDA kernel 专为 16-bit state 设计，采用 FlashInfer `cake_gdn` BF16-state MTP decode 布局，把瓶颈从 state traffic 移向更高效的 reduction；允许 FP16 状态走 fused CUDA 路径，并保持输出与状态 bitwise 一致。  
- **与已有路线差别**：不动 FP32 路径，只针对 BF16/FP16 状态新增 kernel；BF16 状态带宽从约 4.0 提升到 5.8–6.3 TB/s，kernel 速度 1.3–1.6×，E2E decode step 最多 5.3%。  
- **可信程度**：PR body 自述，130 个 pytest 通过；240 例 bitwise 对比 0 mismatched bits；GB300 多 GPU 上 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 E2E 数据显示 step 时间提升；GSM8K 88.02%→87.79% 在噪声内。这些为作者自述，本文未独立复现。  
- **启示**：对 GPU 推理系统，混合线性 attention/Mamba 模型的状态缓存量化（16-bit）与投机解码 MTP decode 的融合是缓解带宽瓶颈的关键路径；VLA 若采用 Mamba 类 recurrent backbone，该 kernel 可提高动作推理频率并减少显存占用；异步控制中低精度状态可能累积误差，需在长时程控制验证漂移；对任务成功率/时间的直接影响未知，应先测长 horizon 任务的状态稳定性。

---

**4. DeepSelect 多波 cluster top-k：针对长尾行的自适应调度**  
- **原始材料**：`[sgl-project/sglang PR] [Perf] [NVIDIA] deep_select: Opt-in multi-wave cluster top-k for long-tailed rows`，发布日期 2026-11-21，GitHub PR，URL：https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51348  
- **旧问题**：DeepSelect bf16 top-k 在 batch 行数超过单波 cluster tier 后降级为 one-CTA-per-row kernel，该 kernel 一次处理所有行，耗时由 batch 中最长行决定；agentic 解码中上下文长度呈长尾分布，最长行可达均值 2.6–6.3 倍，造成尾延迟。  
- **核心技术机制**：新增 opt-in `SGLANG_DEEP_SELECT_MULTIWAVE=1`，当行数超过所有 one-wave tier 且不超过 512 时，将 batch 发送到行数最多的 cluster tier（SM107 上为 2-CTA tier），该 tier 以多波方式运行；每个 row 的 cluster 独立 launch，一个 cluster 退休后硬件立即启动下一个，因此总时间跟随总行长度而非最长行。短行与均匀长度仍走默认内核。  
- **与已有路线差别**：相比 one-CTA-per-row 的“最长行瓶颈”和单波 cluster 的容量限制，多波 cluster 通过复用窄 tier 提高并行度，适合长尾行分布，但 uniform 时可能退化（kernel 时间 +32% 到 +137%）。  
- **可信程度**：PR body 自述，Exactness 按 multiset 匹配 `torch.topk`（0 bad rows）；19 个 GPU 测试通过；相对默认 kernel 的 kernel 时间在长尾分布多为 -20% 至 -59%，但存在退化案例；GSM8K 均值 off 0.902 vs on 0.897，在 run-to-run 噪声内。本文未独立核验。  
- **启示**：对 GPU 推理系统，长尾或不平衡的 per-row 算子（sparse top-k、MoE routing、token selection）可采用多波 cluster 调度来降低尾延迟，但需要运行时判断触发条件，避免均匀流量下的性能损失；VLA 推理中动作 token 候选选择或 tree search 可能有类似 top-k 结构；异步控制的多请求上下文长度异质，多波思想可借鉴；对机器人任务成功率/时间无直接关系，但可降低策略推理尾延迟，提升控制稳定性。

---

**5. DSA metadata kernel 将 batch size 改为 runtime arg，避免 per-bs Triton 重编译**  
- **原始材料**：`[sgl-project/sglang PR] [Fix] dsa: Make metadata kernel batch size a runtime arg to avoid per-bs Triton recompiles`，发布日期 2026-11-21，GitHub PR，URL：https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/50929  
- **旧问题**：三个 DSA attention metadata Triton kernel 把 batch size 声明为 `tl.constexpr`，当 CUDA graph 重放时每个新的 padded batch size 触发一次 JIT 重编译，在 serving loop 内产生首次 decode step 延迟，并使 Triton cache 膨胀。  
- **核心技术机制**：将三个 kernel 的 `bs` 从 `tl.constexpr` 改为 runtime 参数，仅用作循环边界，避免 Triton 为每个 batch size 特化和缓存独立 kernel；语义不变。  
- **与已有路线差别**：不改变 kernel 计算逻辑，只消除编译期维度特化，降低动态 batch 下的 JIT 开销。  
- **可信程度**：PR body 自述，提供 GLM-5 dummy 4-layer 服务的并发 sweep repro 脚本，预填非 Triton JIT；但正文截断，未看到最终性能对比数据。可信为“PR body + 代码变更”，需验证是否完全消除 JIT 及收益幅度。  
- **启示**：对 GPU 推理系统是动态 batch 与 Triton JIT/CUDA graph 交互的典型陷阱：编译期常量特化会破坏预热效果，应区分真正编译期常量与运行期维度；VLA/异步控制里 batch size 可能随传感器触发频繁变化，此类隐藏 JIT 会引入延迟抖动；可反证实验：在不同并发下统计首次 decode step 的 JIT 耗时和 Triton cache 条目数是否恒定。

---

**6. ZAYA1 CCA prefill checkpoints：混合模型的长 prompt 单步 prefill**  
- **原始材料**：`[vllm-project/vllm PR] [Perf][Model] Export ZAYA1 CCA prefill checkpoints`，发布日期 2026-11-21，GitHub PR，URL：https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68921  
- **旧问题**：ZAYA1 hybrid model 的 CCA 层不导出 prefill checkpoint，前缀缓存开启时调度器无法在最后一个 Mamba block 边界拆分 prompt，导致每个长 prompt 多执行一次 prefill step。  
- **核心技术机制**：让 `ZayaCCA` 声明 align-mode checkpoint alignment=1；其状态为最后 `cca_time0 + cca_time1 - 2` 个原始 q/k 输入加前一个 token 的延迟值，在 checkpoint offset 复制到 checkpoint block，纯 PyTorch 实现，无 host sync。每个请求额外预留一个 checkpoint block，占用 0.386% KV-cache token 容量。  
- **与已有路线差别**：此前所有 Mamba 层可导出 checkpoint 才允许 prompt 在 block 边界拆，CCA 层缺失导致额外 prefill；本 PR 补齐该能力，使 8000 token 冷 prompt 从两步（7936+64）变成单步 8000。  
- **可信程度**：PR body 自述，新增测试 `test_zaya_cca_exports_state_at_checkpoint` 在 B300/MI355X/CPU 通过，禁用导出则失败；TTFT 在 B300 降 15–38%，MI355X 降 18–33%；生成 token 在臂内和臂间匹配，最大 logprob 差 0.047/0.089。本文未独立核验。  
- **启示**：对 GPU 推理系统，混合循环/线性 attention 模型的前缀缓存必须完整导出各层状态，否则调度器无法拆分，增加 prefill 步数和 TTFT；对 VLA 长期上下文缓存或机器人轨迹前缀缓存有类似要求，需保证状态导出与重放一致性；异步控制中长时程状态缓存可复用，但需评估同步开销；对任务时间特别是长 horizon 任务可能受益；需要进一步验证 checkpoint block 预留对高并发 KV 容量的实际影响。

---

**跨领域弱信号**  
NAT VLA 的“部分动作 chunk 可执行”与 LLM serving 的 token streaming 正在向同一个方向收敛：把长序列决策拆成可提前执行的前缀。多模态 encoder 的可变形状图化（LFM3-VL）与机器人多传感器异步帧处理面临相同的 runtime shape 问题。长尾请求调度的多波 cluster 思路（DeepSelect）与多机器人控制中的异质上下文队列调度是同一类问题。混合循环模型的 checkpoint 导出与机器人长时程状态缓存也是同构挑战。

**趋势假设**  
1. **面向机器人控制的 VLA 将优先引入 token 级流式动作执行或 prefix chunking，攻击首动作延迟**。置信度：中高（0.7）。可反证实验：在 LIBERO 或真实 manipulation 基准上，比较流式部分动作解码与整 chunk 解码，若任务成功率显著下降且首动作延迟未明显改善，则该方向搁置。  
2. **推理系统 kernel 优化更普遍采用 runtime 分支/多波调度，替代编译期特化，以适应动态 batch 和长尾请求**。置信度：中（0.6）。可反证实验：在均匀流量或短行场景下，runtime 分支/多波内核相比现有路径的性能损失是否能控制在可接受范围；若退化显著，将只作为 opt-in。  
3. **混合循环/线性 attention 模型的长序列部署要求每层可导出 checkpoint，以便前缀缓存单步 prefill**。置信度：中高（0.7）。可反证实验：在多个 hybrid model 上测量 prefill 步数、TTFT 与 KV 容量开销，若 checkpoint block 占用超过一定阈值且缓存命中率提升不足，则选择性启用该能力。

**本周值得精读的 2 篇**  
- NAT VLA（https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/5416）：机器人 VLA 流式动作 token 化的实现与验证，是具身智能与推理系统交叉的重要样本。  
- LFM3-VL encoder CUDA Graph（https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67976）：展示可变形状多模态 encoder 如何通过预计算索引 + fused kernel 实现安全图化，对 VLA 感知模块与 GPU 推理系统均具借鉴意义。

---
**本次采集**：共采集 350 条，去重后 350 条；候选池 120 条，本次精选 9 条。源异常 1 处（见仓库 Actions 日志）。

selected.summary: ## Summary / Motivation Adds **NAT VLA** (`nat_vla`), a vision-language-action policy built on LFM2-VL that writes robot actions as NAT action tokens. NAT is a neural action tokenizer whose tokens are ordered in time and whose decoder is causal, so a chunk's first actions can be decoded and executed while the rest of the chunk is still being generated. The policy can be fine-tuned with `lerobot-train --policy.path=ahad-j/nat-vla-450m`. Note: the pretrained weights (`ahad-j/nat-vla-450m`) and the NAT tokenizer (`ahad-j/nat-tokenizer-h32-l4-c6400`) are not public on the Hub yet. Until they are, the default configuration can't download them, and the released-weights test is skipped. ## Related issues - None. ## What changed - `src/lerobot/policies/nat_vla/nat_tokenizer.py`: the NAT action tokenizer, built from its own `config.json` and `model.safetensors` (swappable with `--policy.action_tokenizer`). It encodes and decodes actions of any number of columns, gives the tokens needed for a number of steps, the first tokens of a chunk that starts with given actions, and a streaming decoder. - `src/lerobot/policies/nat_vla/modeling_nat_vla.py`: the policy. - Training is cross-entropy over the action tokens, with the VLM's original token embeddings frozen. - `select_action` generates greedily in a background thread and returns each latent's actions as soon as its tokens are generated. - `--policy.rtc_steps` turns on token-prefix real-time chunking: the next chunk is generated while the current chunk's last actions run, and starts with their tokens. - `configuration_nat_vla.py`, `processor_nat_vla.py`: the config and the default pre/post-processors (MIN_MAX action normalization). - Registration in `lerobot.policies`, a `nat_vla` extra (transformers only), `docs/source/nat_vla.mdx`, and a model card section. - No changes to existing policies; no breaking changes. ## How was this tested (or how to run locally) - Tests added: `tests/policies/nat_vla/test_nat_vla.py` (24 tests: tokenization of 1 to 2 column groups, streamed prefixes, the streaming decoder, prompt layout, frozen embedding rows, streamed actions equal the predicted chunk, real-time chunking prefixes, config validation, save/reload, swapping in a different NAT tokenizer). `pytest -q tests/policies/nat_vla` - With the released weights on LIBERO frames: - the policy reproduces the original training code's prompt tokens and its training loss (7.621155 against 7.621157 on the same batch); - streamed actions equal the predicted chunk exactly; - the first action arrives in about 40 ms on an RTX 4090. - Real-time chunking in a 30 Hz loop with `n_action_steps=16`, `rtc_steps=8`: - no wait at chunk starts after the first (0.1 ms, against about 40 ms without); - action changes at chunk switches of 0.011 to 0.031, against 0.05 to 0.10 without. - A 100-step `lerobot-train` fine-tune on LIBERO trained, saved, reloaded and predicted actions. ## Checklist (required before merge) - [x] Linting/formatting run (`pre-commit run` on the changed files) - [x] All tests pass locally (`pytest -q tests/policies/nat_vla`) - [x] Documentation updated - [ ] CI is green - [ ] Community Review: I have reviewed another contributor's open PR and linked it here: # ## Reviewer notes - The weights are a derivative of LFM2-VL-450M and are released under the LFM Open License v1.0; the code is Apache 2.0 like the rest of LeRobot. - `transformers` is the only extra dependency (the `nat_vla` extra aliases `transformers-dep`).

selected.summary: ## Overview Add a separate fused GDN MTP decode kernel for 16-bit (BF16/FP16) recurrent state, and let the fused CUDA path take FP16 state (`--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16` falls back to Triton on `main`). At 16 bits the existing kernel is bound by the warp-shuffle reductions, not state traffic: **1.3–1.6×** faster kernel, **up to 5.3%** faster decode steps on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8. The kernel design is adapted from FlashInfer's `cake_gdn` BF16-state MTP decode kernel by @yyihuang, added in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4581 (Apache-2.0, shipped in v0.7.3); credit for the layout goes there. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used. ## Claims - 16-bit state reaches 5.8–6.3 TB/s at 32+ requests (from ~4.0), on par with FP32 state. FP32 state and small batches (V split) still run the existing kernel, unchanged. - **Bitwise-identical** outputs and state to the existing kernel; GSM8K unchanged. - FP16 state now runs the fused CUDA kernel. selected.summary: [by Claude Code] ## Motivation DeepSelect's bf16 top-k sends a batch to a cluster kernel only when the batch fits in one wave of some cluster tier. A larger batch goes to the one-CTA-per-row kernel. That kernel runs every row at once, so its time is set by the longest row in the batch. The DeepSeek-V4.1 decode indexer hits this case. With DSpark (6 verify rows per request) and 40 requests per rank, each index layer runs a top-512 over 240 rows. On a Vera Rubin GPU (SM107, 212 SMs) the widest one-wave tier is the 2-CTA cluster with 106 rows, so all 240 rows go to the one-CTA-per-row kernel. Agentic decode batches mix very different context lengths: in the samples below, the longest row is 2.6-6.3x the mean row. The cluster kernel already launches one cluster per row, and the hardware starts the next row's cluster as an earlier one retires. Run over several waves, its time follows the total row length instead of the longest row. ## Modifications - New opt-in env `SGLANG_DEEP_SELECT_MULTIWAVE=1`. It sends bf16 top-k batches with more rows than every one-wave tier, and at most `_MULTIWAVE_MAX_ROWS` = 512 rows, to the cluster tier with the most rows per wave (the 2-CTA tier on SM107), which then runs over several waves. selected.title: [sgl-project/sglang PR] [Feat] marlin: Run MXFP8 (E4M3 weights, E8M0 group-32 scales) MoE experts on the Marlin kernel
selected.summary: ## Motivation Marlin MoE already runs MXFP4 experts (E2M1 weights, group-32 E8M0 scales) on BF16 activations. MXFP8 MoE checkpoints (E4M3 weights with the same group-32 E8M0 scales) have no W8A16 path on GPUs without a native MXFP8 MoE kernel, so they cannot be served there. This change lets the existing Marlin MoE kernel dequantize E4M3 weights with E8M0 scales. FP8 group-32 weights already have one Marlin path on main: #51302 runs them with 16-bit scales that carry the FP8 exponent bias folded in (`repack_mxfp8` in `inkling2_marlin_sm90.py`, kernels from `FP8G32_GET_IF`). The two formats share every existing dispatch key (`kFE4M3fn`, `group_blocks == 2`), so this change makes the scale type part of the key: the host derives it from the scale tensor, and 16-bit and E8M0 scales each select their own kernels. No caller changes and no flag; the repack decides the scale dtype and the kernel follows it. ## Modifications - `marlin_template.h`: accept `kFE4M3fn` weights with `kFE8M0fnu` scales (group_blocks 2). E8M0 scales do not absorb the FP8 exponent bias the way ordinary FP8 Marlin scales do, so the dequant flop is kept for that combination. - `moe_wna16_marlin.cuh`: `_GET_IF_S` matches a runtime `s_type` alongside the existing keys and `_GET_IF` keeps the default scale-type rule (activation dtype, E4M3 for NVFP4, E8M0 for MXFP4). `FP8G32_GET_IF` stays the 16-bit-scale family and `MXFP8_GET_IF` instantiates the E8M0 variants for `kFE4M3fn` next to the MXFP4 ones (BF16 activations only, same configs). The host derives `b_s_type` from `b_scales` (8-bit means E8M0, accepted only for FP8 group-32 on BF16 activations; otherwise the scales must be 16-bit) and threads it through `marlin_mm` → `determine_exec_config` → `get_marlin_kernel`. - `moe_wna16_marlin.py`: group-32 FP8 scales must be `float8_e8m0fnu` or the activation dtype. - `fused_marlin_moe.py`: recognize 8-bit weights with E8M0 scales as MXFP8 (BF16 activations, no atomic add, same as MXFP4); add `no_combine_keep_router_weight` so a caller can request unweighted per-route rows with `no_combine` (default keeps the current behaviour). - `moe_runner/marlin.py`: forward `no_combine_keep_router_weight` instead of asserting it; the FP16 upcast path covers 8-bit E8M0 weights as well. - `marlin_utils_fp8.py`: `prepare_moe_mxfp8_layer_for_marlin` repacks canonical E4M3 experts and unswizzled group-32 E8M0 scales into the Marlin layouts. - `mxfp4_marlin_moe.py`: `build_marlin_moe_quant_info` takes the weight bit width. No behaviour change for INT4/INT8, NVFP4, MXFP4 or the existing 16-bit-scale FP8 group-32 path: they keep their kernels and configs. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_wna16_marlin.py -k mxfp8`, run on an SM100-class GPU: - `test_fused_marlin_moe_mxfp8` compares the fused Marlin MXFP8 output with a float32 dequantized reference for combined, router-weighted and unweighted routes over several token counts: 20 parametrizations pass. - `test_moe_wna16_marlin_gemm_mxfp8_scale_dtypes` builds one set of FP8 group-32 weights and runs `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` with E8M0 scales (`prepare_moe_mxfp8_layer_for_marlin`) and with folded 16-bit scales (the `repack_mxfp8` recipe), for BF16 and FP16 activations and m = 1 / 123. Each output matches the float32 reference, and the two BF16 outputs are bitwise equal: 4 parametrizations pass. - The `repack_mxfp8` → `gemm` route from `inkling2_marlin_sm90.py` (E=8, N=512, K=1024, top-2, 16-bit scales) runs and produces finite output on this head; `test_marlin_moe_gemv.py` itself skips on non-SM90 GPUs, so it is left to CI's SM90 runners. - The E8M0 fused outputs on this head are bitwise identical to the outputs before the scale-type dispatch was added (20 shape/route combinations, SHA-256 of the output bytes). ## Benchmark

selected.summary: ## 📌 Description Adds `flashinfer.gemv_bf16_fp4_gather` (also `flashinfer.gemm.gemv_bf16_fp4_gather`), a CuTe DSL kernel for SM120/121: ``` out[m, out_col_offset + row_ids[m, j]] = alpha * (a[m] @ dequant(b[row_ids[m, j]])) ``` - `a`: `(M, K)` bf16. `b`: `(R, K/2)` packed E2M1 (low nibble = even column). `b_descale`: `(R, K/16)` E4M3 block scales in the linear layout (from `fp4_quantize(..., is_sf_swizzled_layout=False)`), so each picked row's scales are one contiguous read instead of 4-byte pieces spread across a 128x4 block. `alpha`: optional `(1,)` fp32. - `row_ids`: `(M, J)` int32/int64. Negative ids are skipped. Columns of `out` that no id names are left untouched. - `out`: `(M, N)` bf16/fp16/fp32 with unit inner stride (a strided row view works). fp32 accumulation, one rounding at the store. - CUDA-graph safe: no allocation, no host sync. Use case: sparse LM heads for speculative decoding on bandwidth-bound GPUs. Each draft token computes exact logits only for a dense prefix of the vocabulary (a regular GEMM) plus `J` rows picked by a cheap scorer and `flashinfer.top_k`. This op computes the picked rows and writes them straight into the full-vocabulary logits tensor, so no separate scatter kernel is needed. The consumer is the sparse draft head proposed in vllm-project/vllm#67220. Kernel: no SMEM, no tensor cores. A half-warp streams one row at a time with 16B non-coherent loads (`cvt.rn.f16x2.e2m1x2` / `cvt.rn.f16x2.e4m3x2` decode, fp32 FMA). The token's activation slice stays in registers. Tokens are the fastest grid axis, so CTAs resident at the same time cover the same slot range of every token. When ids are ascending (both `torch.topk(sorted=False)` and `flashinfer.top_k` return them mostly ascending), rows shared between tokens are served from L2. That is where the large-M speedup comes from. Out of scope: the dense prefix GEMM and the scorer (existing GEMMs) and top-k (existing `flashinfer.top_k`). selected.title: [sgl-project/sglang PR] [Feat] speculative: Apply exact per-row sampling penalties in verify
selected.summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #52035. Speculative verify scores several draft positions of a request in one forward, but every verify row of a request got the same penalty: the request's history as of the start of the block. A row at draft depth `d` therefore missed the draft tokens before it on its own path, and `min_new_tokens` was off by `d`. With the history now in a per-request device pool, exactness only needs the same formula applied over the pool counts plus each row's ancestor tokens. This replaces #51903: it covers EAGLE trees and NGRAM as well as DFlash and DSpark, it is exact on every device, and it costs less per step. ## Modifications - **Verify kernel** `sampling.verify_penalties` (JIT, CUDA sm_80+), in `kernels/jit/csrc/sampling/verify_penalties.cuh`. - **Semantics:** verify row `r` of request `i` counts `counts[penalty_index_i]` plus the in-vocab draft tokens on `r`'s path. The root is excluded and `r` itself is included. `min_new_tokens` is gated by `lens + depth(r)`. - **Input:** the tree comes in the verify's own `next_child` / `next_sibling` format; with neither, the block is a chain. - **Layout:** one CTA per (vocab chunk, penalized request, row group). - History counts are read once per chunk and turned into a per-entry base penalty. - Rows are staged with `cp.async` and rewritten with 16-byte vectors. - Entries on a draft path or in the stop set are fixed per row afterwards. - **Numerics:** rows are bitwise equal to non-spec decoding: fp32 table math, one round to the logits dtype after the additive step, and the same `div.full.f32` division that the compiled `apply_scaling_penalties` uses. - **Commit kernel** `sampling.accumulate_penalty_counts`: one launch with exact int32 atomics on `counts` and `lens`. It replaces `index_put_` / `index_add_` on CUDA, with the same out-of-vocab and accept-mask rules. - **`PenaltyStatusPool` keeps each request's params** (frequency, presence, repetition, `min_new_tokens`, padded stop ids) on the device, written at `alloc`. `StepPenalties.build` uploads only the step's indices, in one H2D copy. - **`StepPenalties.apply_verify`** runs the kernel on CUDA sm_80+ and an exact torch fallback elsewhere. - **Hooks**: - EAGLE-family and NGRAM verify pass the draft tree in `eagle_sample`. This covers both post-verify routes. - DFlash and DSpark verify pass the block as a chain. - **DFlash and DSpark verify** now apply the custom logit processor after penalties, the grammar mask and the logit bias, as non-spec sampling does. The logit bias is added in fp32 instead of being cast to the logits dtype first. - **Provider view**: `VerifySamplingView` carries `step_penalties` (`VerifyPenaltiesView`) instead of the two block-start tables, and `MEGAKERNEL_API_VERSION` is now 3. - **Removed**: `apply_acc_penalties`, `has_acc_penalties`, the `acc_additive_penalties` / `acc_scaling_penalties` views, and the table build in `copy_for_forward`. Non-spec tables are built when sampling first reads them. - Host code only arranges indices: no host sync, and no new stream or event. ## Behavior changes - Speculative verify rows with sampling penalties now see their own draft path, so accepted tokens can change versus #52035. - The custom logit processor in DFlash and DSpark verify now runs last, and the bf16 logit bias rounds once instead of twice. - `VerifySamplingView` no longer exposes the two penalty tables. No in-tree provider read them; an out-of-tree provider that did must call `step_penalties.apply_verify`. - On devices without the kernel (non-CUDA, or CUDA below sm_80), verify uses the torch fallback. It is exact but slower, and allocates `[rows, vocab]` temporaries. - A request's stop ids for `min_new_tokens` are read once at admission. ## Follow-up A Triton verify kernel for ROCm and pre-sm_80
